name: Banh trang cuon
summary: Banh trang cuon is boiled pork you roll at the table in rice paper with herbs, then dip. Some shops add steamed scad, cá nục hấp, on the same tray.
origin: Da Nang lunch rooms. The plate is built to share, with the herbs and the rice paper in separate piles.
howToEat: Take a sheet, add pork and herbs, roll, then dip. Ask what is in the bowl if you do not eat fermented fish.
When the shop has cá nục hấp, roll the steamed fish the same way. It is the same lunch, not a second menu.
Eat it sitting down at lunch. It is a slow plate.
The Da Nang roll is pork, herbs, and mắm nêm, with a sheet of mì lá under the rice paper before the herbs and the pork.

In Hoi An, the Hoi An World Heritage conservation centre’s 7 June 2023 list describes a grilled-pork roll: herbs, star fruit or sour pineapple, green banana, a thin rice-paper sheet, a little bún, and fish sauce or mắm nêm. It is the grilled plate, not the boiled Da Nang lunch. The hour is Check on arrival.
where: Bà Hường is at 364 đường 3/2, with a Duy Tân branch near the airport. Trần is at 4 Lê Duẩn. Both are pork-and-rice-paper lunches.
In Hoi An, the grilled roll. A street and the hour are Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Banh trang cuon — Da Nang pork rice-paper rolls
seoDescription: Roll boiled pork and herbs in rice paper, then dip. Ba Huong is at 364 duong 3/2 in Da Nang, with steamed scad on the same tray, and Tran is at 4 Le Duan.
